messages.author: 563435cd1cb6a261
messages.subject: Counter Reactivity
parts:
Hi,

What I'd like to do is have a form submit when clicked it will load a
different URI using the form input values to build the URI:

When on http://example.org/foo/bar/baz output consists of analysis which
uses the values foo, bar, baz - This is something I can do now.

I'd like to bring in the following:

While on that page, when the input values are changed and the form
submit button is clicked, URI should change to
http://example.org/qux/bbq/omg (where qux, bbq, omg are from inputs). It
doesn't matter whether this is with AJAX and History API, or a new GET
to the page (but I slightly prefer this)

When the new page is loaded, I'd like to do the same as I did for
/foo/bar/baz and load the output using the values from the URI.

Does this mean that I have to move away from reactivity? What would be
the painless way of going at it?

-Sarven
http://csarven.ca/#i

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Counter Reactivity
parts:
You can achieve what you are seeking with Shiny by passing the parameters as a Query String (see this tutorial here 
http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#client-data). 

http://example.org/?arg1=foo&arg2=bar&arg3=baz

I don't think Shiny can server arbitrary pages as it will mess up resource paths.  By going down the queryString route, I think you will still get caching, history and the likes of it.

messages.subject: Re: Counter Reactivity
parts:
Resource paths can be dealt with in a similar way to query paths by
simply taking the url_pathname and splitting it up. With reverse proxy,
this works fine. Caching and reactivity works fine too.

What I'm trying to resolve is to submit a GET with the new input
selections. I imagine I could do this by overriding the existing
behaviour (which doesn't sound right to me at the moment but I'd like to
be convinced otherwise if that is indeed the way to go), but I'm looking
for a way that's probably simpler with Shiny.

-Sarven
